content.title: Johnny Dawkins Has Changed the Narrative at UCF  Now the Knights Must Decide His Future
content.text: About 10 months ago, the outlook for UCF men's basketball was less than stellar.The Knights closed the 2024 regular season at 16–15, including a 7–13 finish in the Big 12. Then, after edging Utah in the opening round of the conference tournament, UCF pushed Kansas to overtime before falling short. Soon after, leading scorer Keyshawn Hall opted out of postseason play and entered the transfer portal, leaving the Knights shorthanded for the inaugural College Basketball Crown tournament.Many fans openly questioned whether Johnny Dawkins — UCF's head coach since 2016 — should be relieved of his duties. Meanwhile, his supporters countered that Dawkins was working with limited resources in one of the nation's toughest leagues, and expectations needed to be recalibrated accordingly.Fast forward to today, and the conversation has flipped entirely.Momentum Turned into BeliefEven without Hall, UCF surged through the CBC, winning three straight games and reaching the championship game before falling to Nebraska. That unexpected run has proven to be a turning point.Dawkins has since carried that momentum straight into the 2025 season, completely retooling the roster and watching it click almost immediately. After a statement win over No. 11 Texas Tech last weekend, the Knights sit at 17–4 overall and 6–3 in Big 12 play — and are one of the league's most surprising contenders.National voices have taken notice:Dick Vitale: "Wow, tip the hat to Coach Johnny Dawkins … The first star of the Coach K era was Dawkins… Johnny is #awesomebaby."Jon Rothstein: "That's the resume of an NCAA Tournament team."Jeff Goodman: "One of the biggest surprises of the season … Incredible job by Dawkins and his staff."With marquee home wins over Kansas and Texas Tech plus a road victory at Texas A&M, UCF no longer looks like a perennial rebuilding project; it looks like a legitimate NCAA Tournament squad.The Contract Question Looms LargeThat brings us to the elephant in the room. In June 2024, UCF Athletic Director Terry Mohajir extended Dawkins' contract by two years through the 2026–27 season, a move that drew mixed reactions from the fan base at the time. Dawkins makes $2.1 million this season with the chance to also earn relatively modest on-court performance and team academic bonuses, and while his salary rises to $2.2 million next year, that figure is not guaranteed.So what happens next?Does UCF view this season as a perfect storm and choose to wait before committing further? Or does Mohajir recognize the risk of standing pat, knowing Dawkins could be hired away this offseason with no buyout attached?"As always, we do not discuss coaching contracts or any negotiations publicly, particularly during the season. We are proud of the success Johnny and our men's basketball team are having and remain fully committed to supporting him, his staff, and our players as they move forward through the rest of the season," a UCF Athletics spokesperson told Knights247 earlier this week.If the season ended today, Dawkins would be a strong candidate for Big 12 Coach of the Year — and coaches with that résumé rarely linger without security.Dawkins' Perspective Matters, TooAt 62 years old, Dawkins has options — and priorities —that extend beyond the numbers.He may prefer stability and choose to remain at UCF, even at a below-market salary. Then again, he may feel frustrated by a segment of the UCF fanbase that underestimates how difficult it is to compete in the Big 12 with a comparatively modest NIL budget. He could even choose to pursue one final payday elsewhere before retirement.Or, in a move that would surprise many, he could decide this season is the perfect capstone to a long and respected career.A Program at a CrossroadsWhat is clear is this: Johnny Dawkins has earned the benefit of the doubt.He has rebuilt belief inside the program, elevated UCF's national profile, and shown that winning basketball is possible in Orlando — even against the giants of the Big 12. Whatever decision comes next will say a great deal about how UCF views its basketball future.Since arriving at UCF in 2016-17, Dawkins has compiled a record of 185-124 (a .599 winning clip) and has had only one overall losing season, the 2020-2021 year that saw a reduced schedule and significant disruptions due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Still, while Dawkins' teams have enjoyed postseason play in many of his years at the helm of the Knights, he has produced only one NCAA tournament team during that time.One thing, at least, feels certain. Johnny Dawkins is a good man, a proven leader, and one of college basketball's most genuine figures. And while it's always good to see good things happen to good people, it would feel awfully strange if his best-ever year at UCF turned out to be his last.For more UCF coverage, follow Knights247 on X, Instagram, and Facebook!Sign up for our FREE UCF Knights Newsletter
